title: Detection, sorting, and immortalization of dual expresser lymphocytes from human peripheral blood samples
protocol: Stain PBMCs with a cocktail of 4-fluorophore-conjugated antibodies specific for CD19, CD5, IgD, and TCRαβ.
Prepare compensation control tubes: stain samples with single fluorophore antibodies and leave one sample unstained.
Label FACS tubes with permanent marker.
Add 1 to 2 million cells in 100 μL to each FACS tube.
Stain the sample with Live/Dead dye of choice if desired, using PI at 1 μg/mL or Live/Dead Aqua at 1 μL per mL PBS.
Prepare a single-color compensation control for the Live/Dead dye if used.
Mix 5 μL of each fluorophore-conjugated antibody specific for TCRαβ, IgD, CD5, and CD19 with the stained sample in FACS buffer to reach a final volume of 100 μL.
Vortex the tubes containing the samples and incubate on ice for 20–30 min, protected from light.
Wash the samples and controls with 2–3 mL of FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the washed samples at 525 xg (1500 rpm) and discard the supernatants.
Resuspend samples in 600 μL of FACS buffer.
Vortex tubes.
Move to your FACS instrument and perform compensation setup using your compensation controls.
Run your samples and acquire 500,000–1,000,000 events per sample when possible.
Export the FCS files.
Open FlowJo and drag your FCS files into the application.
Open your sample files.
Gate total lymphocytes using the FSC-Area vs SSC-Area plot.
Gate on single cells and exclude doublets using the FSC-Area vs FSC-Height followed by SSC-Area vs SSC-Height plots.
Alternatively, doublets can be excluded by using FSC-Height vs FSC-Width and SSC-Height vs SSC-Width plots.
If you stained your samples with Live/Dead, gate on live cells using a histogram of the Live/Dead staining as recommended by the manufacturer.
Draw a 2-parameter dot plot using CD5 vs CD19.
Gate on Bcon (CD5− CD19+).
Gate on Tcon (CD5+ CD19−).
Gate on the CD5+ CD19+ subpopulations.
Prepare a single-cell suspension of PBMCs from T1D patients initially suspended in 500 μL FACS buffer.
Use approximately 50 × 10^6 fresh PBMCs for the experiment.
Reserve about 50 μL (approximately 5 × 10^6 cells) to prepare single color compensation and unstained controls.
Use the remaining 45 × 10^6 cells in 450 μL FACS buffer for sorting DEs.
Stain PBMCs using a four-antibody cocktail as described in Part I: Identifying DEs by flow cytometry.
Prepare single-color compensation control tubes by pipetting 10 μL of PBMC suspension (5 × 10^5 cells) into each tube.
Add 90 μL FACS buffer to each compensation control tube for a total volume of 100 μL.
Label the unstained control tube and prepare it similarly as above.
Stain the sorting sample using 20 μL of each fluorophore-conjugated antibody.
Stain the compensation control tubes using 5 μL of antibody.
Gently vortex each FACS tube to mix cells and achieve homogeneous staining.
Incubate the tubes for 20 min on ice or at 4°C, protected from light.
Wash samples at least three times using 2–3 mL of FACS buffer each time.
Resuspend the sorting sample into a total volume of 3 mL in FACS buffer.
Resuspend each compensation control sample into a total volume of 500 μL of FACS buffer.
Filter the “sort sample” using a FACS tube with a 35 μm cell strainer cap to eliminate residual cell clumps.
Add PI stock solution at a concentration of 1 mg/mL to identify and exclude dead cells, aiming for a final dilution of 1–2 μg/mL.
Acquire approximately 10,000 events from each compensation tube to perform compensation setup.
Finalize the compensation using the fully-stained sample and make any necessary adjustments.
Set up your sorter for sorting with a 70 μm nozzle, sheath pressure of 60 psi, and drop drive frequency of 95–98 kHz.

Sort your sample into three or four subpopulations depending on whether DEs are sorted as separate (IgD+ and IgD−) subsets or as one mixed population. The other two subpopulations are Bcon and Tcon cells.
Sort DEs (IgD+ and IgD−) into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes containing about 700–800 μL of lymphocyte collection medium.
Sort Bcon and Tcon cells into 5 mL polypropylene tubes containing 1 mL of lymphocyte collection medium.
Re-run an aliquot of sorted DE cells on the sorter using the original gating strategy.
Determine the percentage of DE cells in the sorted sample by using the same gating strategy.
Sort DE lymphoblastoid cell lines and clones using Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) under sterile conditions in a biosafety cabinet.
Thaw 1 vial of irradiated-fibroblasts (ATCC 055-X) using the specified method.
Resuspend fibroblasts to a density of 2.5 × 10^5 cells/mL using CTM.
Gently mix the resuspended cells by pipetting up and down with a serological pipette.
Plate 200 μL of irradiated-fibroblasts onto each well of a 96-well flat bottom tissue-culture plate, containing 50,000 cells per well.
Incubate the tissue culture plate overnight (18 hours) at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2.
Sort DEs using the specified method from freshly isolated PBMCs.
Prepare infectious medium by diluting 1 mL of EBV solution to 30% in CTM containing 2.5 μg/mL CpG ODN 2006 (ODN7909).
Suspend sorted DEs in the prepared infectious medium.
Seed DEs onto the fibroblast feeder layers using 50 or 100 DE cells per well.
Check cultures for DE growth from day 3 to day 7.
Check cultures on a daily basis under light microscope for cell growth and any sign of contamination.
Replace half of the spent medium with fresh infectious medium when cell density reaches 80%–90%.
Typically, replenish culture medium every 5–7 days as needed.
Transfer contents into wells of 24-well tissue culture plate as cultures expand.
Transfer contents onto wells of 6-well plates as cells continue to grow.
Subculture on fibroblast feeding layers optionally to enhance viability and growth.
Expand cultures to 75–100 mL using flasks over the next few weeks.
Store generated LCLs at −80°C or liquid nitrogen.
Use LCL to generate single DE clones using standard limiting dilution methods.
Serially dilute and seed 10, 3.3, 1.1, and 0.33 DEs onto fibroblast-coated 96-well microplates with 100 μL of CpG 2006 containing CTM.
Centrifuge cells at 500 × g for 5–6 minutes at room temperature when freezing down cells.
Remove supernatants and re-suspend cell pellets in cold freezing media at 0.5–1× 10^7 cells/ml.
Place tubes in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage or -80°C for short-term storage.
